items.prompt: In the edit branch of handleEntrySubmit, `updated` is built as `{ ...existing, ...entry, id: existing.id, category }`. What breaks if `id: existing.id` is deleted from that literal?
items.answer: The record keeps its place in the list: it is silently re-keyed to the new `expense-<uuid>` id
distractors: A duplicate row appears: `map` appends the updated record rather than replacing the existing one
Nothing changes: `...existing` is spread first and its id wins over the one in `entry`
The save throws: localStorage rejects two expenses that have different ids for the same row
items.explanation: Later spread keys win: `...entry` carries a new id minted before the mode is known (app.js:193-199). `map` still replaces at the old position, so there is no duplicate, only a changed identity.

items.prompt: The create branch builds `next` with `structuredClone(state)`, while the edit branch gets away with `{ ...state, expenses: state.expenses.map(...) }`. Why can't the create branch use a shallow spread too?
items.answer: It pushes onto arrays and bumps nested goal fields, so any shallow copy would mutate live state
distractors: structuredClone is faster than spreading once the state holds several separate collections of rows
A shallow spread would drop the default budgets that loadState merged into the state object
localStorage.setItem can only serialize objects that were produced by structuredClone
items.explanation: `next.expenses.push(...)`, `goal.current += ...` and `account.balance += ...` would reach the shared arrays/objects of the published `state` with a shallow copy; test 3 fails if you swap it in.

items.prompt: While editing an expense, `localStorage.setItem` throws (quota exceeded). Given the order of operations in the edit branch, what does the user end up with?
items.answer: The dialog stays open with 'Could not save', and memory, storage and screen keep the old expense
distractors: The dialog closes and the row shows the new amount until the next page reload quietly reverts it
The new amount is published to state first, then render() rolls it back from localStorage
The form resets to blank and an uncaught quota exception is logged to the browser console
items.explanation: The write happens inside `try` BEFORE `state = next`; the catch sets the message and returns, so nothing visible changed and the user can retry.

items.prompt: Delete is clicked while `setItem` throws. The handler is `state.expenses = state.expenses.filter(...); saveState(); render();`. Which statement describes the aftermath?
items.answer: Memory drops it, storage keeps it, and the row stays on screen: render() is never reached
distractors: Memory, storage and screen all agree: the expense is gone, and only a reload brings it back
Nothing changes anywhere: filter only runs after saveState has succeeded first
Storage drops the expense, memory keeps it, and the row stays visible: a reload is needed
items.explanation: The mutation on line 584 IS the publication; the exception from saveState (line 585) escapes the listener before render() (line 586), giving three different answers to 'does e1 exist?'.

items.prompt: Viewing July, you edit an expense and change its date to 2026-08-05. The row disappears from the table. What actually happened?
items.answer: Nothing was deleted, as each render re-filters state by month prefix, so the row now belongs to August
distractors: The edit created a new August record with a fresh id and deleted the original July record
July's stored totals were decremented, and the row is hidden until they are recalculated on the next reload
The table caches rows per month, so the edited expense was evicted from July's cached rows
items.explanation: No total is stored; getViewData filters `state` with `item.date.startsWith(month)` (app.js:304) on every render().

items.prompt: You mark a bill paid while viewing July, then switch the month picker to August. What happens to August's 'spent' KPI, and why?
items.answer: It rises: bills are filtered by owner only, and paid bills count toward every month's spending
distractors: It is unchanged: bills are filtered by the dueDay of whichever month is currently being viewed
It drops: paying the bill moves its amount into July's history and out of August's
It is unchanged: paid bills only feed the open-bills KPI and never the spent total
items.explanation: `const bills = state.bills.filter(ownerMatches)` has no month filter, and `expenseTotal = sum(expenses) + sum(paidBills)`. The guide flags it as a product question.

items.prompt: A test sets `#entryAmount` (an `<input type="number">`) to `abc` and dispatches `submit` directly. Which validation message appears, and why?
items.answer: The 'greater than zero' message: the input reads back as an empty string, and Number('') is 0
distractors: The two-decimals message: NaN fails the cents tolerance check that runs on the parsed amount
No message at all: NaN compares false against both of the range bounds used in the check
The invalid-date message: validation aborts on the first non-numeric field it finds
items.explanation: The browser (and jsdom) sanitize a number input before app.js reads it; dispatching submit skips interactive constraint validation, so validateEntry sees 0.

items.prompt: validateEntry rejects more than two decimals with `Math.abs(amount * 100 - Math.round(amount * 100)) > 0.00001` rather than a strict `!==`. What would a strict comparison get wrong?
items.answer: It would reject ordinary prices such as 8.2: 8.2 * 100 is 819.9999999999999
distractors: It would accept 1.005: Math.round rounds the half-cent up to a whole number of cents
It would let three-decimal amounts through: 1.001 passes without any error message
It would reject whole-dollar amounts: Math.round returns a string for integers
items.explanation: Binary floats cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly; the tolerance absorbs that error. Integer cents (05 Exercise 7) removes the problem class.

items.prompt: validateEntry checks the date against `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/` and then compares `new Date(...).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` with the input. What does the second check catch that the regex cannot?
items.answer: Impossible dates such as 2026-02-30, which Date rolls into March so the round trip never matches
distractors: Local-time dates that must be converted to UTC before being written into localStorage
Leap days such as 2028-02-29, which the regex accepts but the Date constructor cannot parse
A time-of-day suffix that the native date input appends to the submitted value on some browsers
items.explanation: The regex only validates shape; the toISOString() round trip is the 'real calendar date' check, step 5 of the fixed validation order.

items.prompt: A create fails at the storage write and the user presses Save again. Harmless locally, but if this submit were a POST to a server, what is the risk the trace lab points at?
items.answer: Each retry mints a new id, so without a reused idempotency key the server could save it twice
distractors: The retry resends the discarded `next` object, so the server would receive a stale copy of state
Ids are derived from the description, so the server would reject the retry as a conflict
The failed write leaves a half-saved document on the server that the retry then overwrites
items.explanation: The id is minted at line 194 during normalization; a failure discards `next` and that id, so the client must reuse one key across retries.

items.prompt: Close and Cancel shut the dialog without resetting `editingExpenseId`. Why is that harmless today, and what change would turn it into a data-loss bug?
items.answer: The Add button resets the flag first, and any other opener that skipped it would overwrite an expense
distractors: editExpense clears the flag whenever the dialog closes, so no opener can ever inherit edit mode
The flag lives on the dialog element and is discarded when the dialog closes, so adding stays safe
render() resets the flag on every redraw, so a stale value never survives into the next click
items.explanation: Mode is decided in one variable and must be reset everywhere the form can be reopened (line 157 today); Close/Cancel (164-165) leave it set.

items.prompt: In a node:test run, an unguarded writer throws a quota error inside a click listener. What does the test run report if the test only clicks?
items.answer: jsdom prints 'Error: Uncaught [Error: quota]', but the test passes unless it asserts on state
distractors: The test fails: the uncaught quota error from the listener is reported as its failure
node:test retries the listener once: the test passes if the second storage write succeeds
The test hangs until its timeout: the click listener never settles after it throws
items.explanation: jsdom reports listener exceptions to its console instead of failing the test; characterization tests must assert on all three stores explicitly.

items.prompt: A change breaks the spending chart, yet `npm test` stays green. Why can the four tests never catch a Chart.js regression?
items.answer: runScripts is 'outside-only', so the Chart.js CDN script never runs and upsertChart exits early
distractors: jsdom snapshots strip canvas pixels, so the chart is drawn but its output can never be compared
The tests stub out render() and only recompute the KPI text nodes, so no chart code runs
package.json's test script swaps Chart.js for a no-op mock module before the test suite runs
items.explanation: With `window.Chart` undefined, `if (!canvas || !window.Chart) return;` exits; the guide lists chart rendering under 'What the tests do not prove'.

items.front: Reset, Delete and the bill-paid toggle each do `mutate state; saveState(); render();` (app.js:150-151, 584-585, 633-635). Storage is full, so setItem throws. What goes wrong?
items.back: State changes but storage does not, and render() is skipped because the exception escapes the listener: memory, storage and screen disagree, and a reload silently undoes the change. Fix: build a full replacement `next`, write it first, publish only on success (a shared commitState(next) helper), and tell the user on failure.

items.front: validateEntry (app.js:786-797) checks amount, decimals, description and date, but not category. Setting `#entryCategory` to a value outside the generated options (e.g. 'Travel') reads back as ''.
items.back: The expense is saved with category '' and its spending disappears from every budget bar. Fix: validate the category against the options updateCategoryOptions produced, not merely that it is non-empty.

items.front: Row buttons interpolate ids raw into attributes (`data-edit-expense="${expense.id}"`, app.js:570-571, 615), and loadState (app.js:176-180) trusts whatever JSON is in localStorage.
items.back: A hand-edited or imported document can inject markup through an id attribute. App-minted UUIDs are safe, stored data is not. Fix: pass ids through the existing escapeHtml (app.js:765) like every other interpolated field.

items.front: Two tabs are open. Each keeps its own in-memory `state` and saves by writing the whole document (saveState, app.js:186-188); nothing listens for the `storage` event.
items.back: Last save wins: one tab silently overwrites the other tab's edits. Fix: listen for `storage` events and reload or merge before writing, or persist per record instead of the whole document.

items.front: You refactor the bill-paid toggle (app.js:631-637) to clone state, set `paid`, and call commitState(next); on failure it returns before render().
items.back: The checkbox still shows the new checked state, so the screen disagrees with state and storage. Fix: revert the control itself (`input.checked = !input.checked`) before returning, because no render() will correct the DOM.
